name: tpl-chain-response-3-goal
task: Carry the box to the exit. If the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move.
error: Task 1 was not accepted within 10 attempts. Last critic feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: `Response(box_fell, holding_box)` is not the stated next-move rule; it only requires carrying the box on that step or later. Replace it with hard `ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box)`. The other clauses correctly require reaching the exit while carrying the box.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) cannot express the task’s “pick it up again on your very next move”: holding_box is a lasting condition, not a one-step pickup event. It requires the box to be held on the next step, which can be satisfied without picking it up then. Use a proposition and clause that represent the pickup action on the next step.

CHANGES REQUIRED: `Response(at_exit, holding_box)` does not enforce carrying the box when reaching the exit; it allows picking the box up afterward. Replace it with a clause that requires `holding_box` on the exit step (for example, `Response` has the wrong semantics here). Keep the hard `Existence(at_exit)` and `ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box)`, which captures the required next-step pickup.

CHANGES REQUIRED: ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) requires the box to be carried on the very next step after it falls, but the task says to pick it up on that move. `holding_box` is a persistent condition, so this clause requires pickup one step too early and can make the task fail. Replace it with ChainResponse(box_fell, a one-step pickup event); `holding_box` should remain required at the exit.

CHANGES REQUIRED: ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) requires the box to be back in your hands on the very next step, but the task says to pick it up again on your very next move. A turn or other action could occur between the fall and that move, so this clause imposes a stricter timing requirement than the task. Use Response(box_fell, holding_box) instead.
